title: LLM Request v1
description: A closed provider-agnostic request configuration for one bounded language-model completion. Source-bearing values may be literal strings or repository-approved file references resolved by the runtime; credentials, when supplied, remain in memory and are never persisted, logged, prompted, or returned.

schema.description: The versioned identifier for this normalized LLM request contract.

provider.description: Provider adapter identity. Registered adapters are claude (the Claude Code CLI) and openrouter. The runtime defaults this field to claude when it is omitted.

model.description: Provider-specific model identifier. When omitted, the runtime uses the provider's default model: sonnet for claude and openai/gpt-5.6-luna for openrouter.

thinking.description: Provider-independent reasoning effort. Adapters translate this value into provider-specific settings; the runtime defaults it to high.

maxFailedAttempts.description: Maximum number of provider invocations that fail before returning a provider or exhausted-attempts result. The runtime defaults this field to 3.

maxIterations.description: Maximum number of successful provider roundtrips, including correction requests after schema-invalid output. The runtime defaults this field to 3.

credentials.description: Optional in-memory provider credentials. The provider adapter may fall back to provider-specific environment variables when this field is omitted; implementations must not persist, log, prompt, or return these values.

oneOf.description: Plain-text task content or a repository-approved file reference.
Structured task data. When taskSchema is configured, this object must validate against it.

task.description: Task data supplied as plain text, a permitted text-file reference, or a structured JSON object. Structured tasks remain objects at the request boundary.

systemPrompt.description: Optional system-level instructions passed separately to the provider rather than embedded in the composed llmPrompt XML. When omitted or null, the provider adapter may omit the system message or apply a provider-specific fallback.
examples: You are an SDLC assessment agent. Return only JSON that conforms to outputSchema.

taskSchema.description: Optional inline task-data JSON Schema object. The task value is validated directly against this schema before provider invocation.

files.description: Ordered repository-approved reference files. Text files are included in the composed llmPrompt; binary files are encoded as base64 and supplied to compatible providers as attachments.

items.description: One ordered reference-file declaration included in the composed prompt.

examples.name: assessment-process
examples.purpose: Define assessment evidence and provider-fallback boundaries.

examples.name: assessment-process
examples.purpose: Define assessment evidence and provider-fallback boundaries.

outputSchema.description: Optional inline required-response JSON Schema object. Provider output must be JSON and must validate against it before a successful response is returned.

messages.description: Optional ordered provider-neutral continuation history. The initial task, taskSchema, and generated prompt remain separate request context.

toolOptions.description: Optional tool-capable completion settings. Its presence selects tool-capable behavior.

tools.description: Ordered declarations of tools the model may request.

autoInvoke.description: Whether the runtime invokes validated tool calls automatically.

maxRounds.description: Maximum number of ordered tool-call batches.

maxCalls.description: Maximum number of individual tool calls across the completion.

Credentials.description: In-memory provider credential material accepted at the request boundary. The object intentionally permits only generic adapter inputs and must never be persisted, logged, placed in prompts, or returned.

apiKey.description: Provider API key held in memory for the duration of the request; it is redacted from diagnostics and excluded from all durable artifacts.

accessToken.description: Provider access token held in memory for the duration of the request; it is redacted from diagnostics and excluded from all durable artifacts.

ReferenceFile.description: Metadata for one ordered regular reference file resolved through the runtime's mediated read boundary. type is the file MIME type; binary files are normalized with base64 encoding.

name.description: Stable prompt-local label for the reference file.

path.description: Repository-relative regular-file path resolved by the mediated source boundary; absolute paths, traversal, and environment-file names are rejected by the runtime.

type.description: MIME type of the referenced file.

encoding.description: Optional content encoding override. When omitted, text MIME types use utf8 and binary MIME types use base64.

purpose.description: Human-readable reason this file is supplied to the model.
examples: Define assessment evidence and provider-fallback boundaries.

examples.name: assessment-process
examples.purpose: Define assessment evidence and provider-fallback boundaries.

inputSchema.description: JSON text containing the tool argument schema.

ToolDefinition.description: A bounded tool declaration available to the model.

content.description: Assistant text, or null when the assistant emitted tool calls.

toolCalls.description: Tool calls emitted by this assistant message.

toolCallId.description: Assistant tool-call identifier receiving this result.

ChatMessage.description: One ordered provider-neutral system, user, assistant, or tool message.

id.description: Stable provider or runtime call identifier.

arguments.description: Parsed JSON object of tool arguments.

ToolCall.description: A normalized assistant tool call retained in canonical history.

taskSchema.description: The structured input for one bounded SDLC assessment.

outputSchema.description: The structured result of one bounded SDLC assessment.
